Its experiment selects three microorganisms: the positive soil result concerns a sterile microcosm at 20 C after 29 days, followed by three-day culture-out before isotope measurement, not direct field flux or all 158 isolates. full_text_inspection.scope: Direct institutional abstract, Crossref abstract/identity metadata, reprint text through interfaces section, and actual PDF pages 1 and 3 (printed S1284/S1286) including Table 2. Remaining images/tables and full bibliography not reviewed.
full_text_inspection.findings: Terminological review, not experimental replication. Its strict nutritional sense requires detrimental nutrient acquisition from a fungal host; association alone is insufficient. Necrotrophy includes host killing before utilization. Intraspecific interactions are allowed. Historical examples include oomycetes, so modern fungal scope needs qualification. Biotrophic hosts need not show overt early disease. No universal penetration, obligacy or molecular mechanism inferred.
full_text_inspection.status_limits: Crossref has no relation/update-to entry in this response; not exhaustive correction/retraction clearance. Qualified DOI AND SRC:MED returned zero hits, not proof of global non-indexing.

full_text_inspection.version: Corneo 2013 thesis, chapter 3; journal-version equivalence not established.
full_text_inspection.inspected: PDF pages 62-79 main text; selected table text pages 86/89; actual pages 69/73/75/86/89 including Figure 2 and selected Tables 1/3. Other chapters, Figure 1, complete taxon tables and raw data not reviewed.
full_text_inspection.assessment: Viable labelled host inocula, isotope enrichment and growth inhibition support host-derived nutrition with harm. Washing and host-specific PCR address contamination; negative amplification does not prove absolute absence. Leached metabolites versus direct parasitism remain partly interpretive. Microcosms use sterilized soil and culture-out before isotope measurement, not intact field flux. Table accessions identify BLAST references, not isolate sequences. Growth inhibition conflicts: abstract 80%, Results 88%, Table 1 80%, with different errors. Microcosm controls and sampling days also differ between prose and tables/figure. Nonsignificance is not equivalence. Chitinase readout measures N-acetylglucosaminidase, not an identified causal enzyme. Authors overlap 2012; thesis is not additional replication.

No exact orphan node or same-scope synonym requiring an existing-record edit was identified in the inspected matches.

The inspected identity and engineering-design sections describe a bacterial consortium and include mycophagy as an assay endpoint. This is community-level bacterial evidence, not an exact fungal TraitRecord. No new feeding claim is inferred from the endpoint list.

PMID35992653 matches a bibliography title; PMID40508300 a predicted-guild comparison; PMID41454778 a bacterial-mycophagy bibliography item; PMID41821943 a discussion-level Trichoderma mechanism statement. These retained reference texts are research leads, not canonical trait records or newly verified primary evidence. No scientific audit of those entire papers is claimed.

Four research/scouting paths and eleven tmp scouting paths repeat two truncated forms of the same citrus consortium lead, PMID42054761. neighbors.label: bacterial mycophagy
neighbors.definition: A trophic-ecology phenotype in which a bacterium actively obtains nutrients from living fungi or oomycetes and uses them for its own growth.

neighbors.label: parasitism
neighbors.definition: A symbiosis in which the microorganism benefits at the expense of its host's fitness, deriving resources from the host while causing it harm.

neighbors.label: symbiosis
neighbors.definition: An ecological lifestyle in which a microorganism lives in persistent physical association with a host or partner organism. It encompasses mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism, which form an evolutionary continuum.

neighbors.label: predatory bacterium
neighbors.definition: A trophic-ecology lifestyle in which a bacterium actively kills and consumes other bacteria for nutrients, e.g. the periplasmic predator Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus.

neighbors.label: saprotrophy
neighbors.definition: A trophic-ecology lifestyle in which an organism feeds on dead or decaying organic matter, mineralizing it and driving carbon and nutrient cycling (decomposition).

neighbors.label: microbial haustorium formation
neighbors.definition: A morphological phenotype in which a fungus or oomycete forms specialized hyphal outgrowths, called haustoria, that establish intimate interfaces with living host cells.

neighbors.label: phenotype
neighbors.definition: A quality that differentiates specific instances of a species from other instances of the same species.

scope_acceptance.decision: Accept concept for one guarded PROPOSED record, subject to fresh reservation gates; not human sign-off or discovery exhaustion.
scope_acceptance.label: nutritional fungal mycoparasitism
scope_acceptance.definition: An ecological phenotype in which a fungus obtains nutrients at the expense of another fungus, either from the living host or after killing it.
scope_acceptance.rationale: A reusable trophic interaction phenotype, not an isolate observation, sequence feature, kit row or precomposed chemical-use pair. Jeffries supports the strict nutritional sense and biotrophic/necrotrophic scope; Pellegrini studies supply host-derived isotope assimilation, with the 2013 source also reporting growth inhibition. Shared authorship is not independent-laboratory replication. Existing bacterial mycophagy and haustorium morphology are not exact equivalents.
scope_acceptance.scope_limits: Fungal actor and host, excluding oomycetes despite historical usage. Require host harm and nutrition, not mere association, inhibition, passive exudate use or unrelated dead-biomass feeding. Killing, penetration, obligacy and a universal molecular mechanism are not required. Phenotype parent avoids importing the local parasitism/symbiosis persistent-association constraint; preserve the attributed hierarchy question.
scope_acceptance.evidence_limits: One native UNRESOLVED review quote is an exact direct institutional abstract match. 2012 is a MED scientific abstract; journal full text unread. 2013 native VERIFIED comes from AGR:IND500606635, not PubMed; the same quote matches the direct institutional abstract. The thesis supplies qualified methods context, not presumed identical journal text or extra replication. Preserve its numerical and assay discrepancies, source-version limits and unavailable publisher notice checks.
